title: Taking away by counting back
examples: How do I subtract on a number line?

explain.say: You have 15 grapes and you eat 6. Yum! How many are left? Look at the number line. We start at 15, and this time the hops go backwards, down to 9.
Put your finger on 15. That is how many grapes you start with. Taking away means fewer, so we hop to the left, where numbers get smaller. Which number comes just before 15?
Hop back 5 times: 14, 13, 12, 11, 10. See? 15 take away 5 lands on 10, a nice tidy ten. But you ate 6 grapes, not 5. How many more hops do we need?
One more hop takes us to 9. So 15 take away 6 equals 9. You ate 6 grapes, and 9 are left. Can you check it by hopping forward 6 from 9?
You are a super hopper! Going back to 10 first is the same make-ten trick that helps you add. Look: 13 take away 4 is back 3 to 10, then 1 more to 9. Try 16 take away 7!

faq.a: Counting back means starting at a number and counting down. For 15 take away 6, you count 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9.

faq.q: How do I subtract on a number line?
faq.a: Put your finger on the first number and hop left once for each number you take away. Where you land is the answer.
asks: How do I take away on a number line?

faq.a: 15 take away 6 is 9. Count back 6 hops from 15: 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9.

faq.q: Why do I hop to the left?
faq.a: On a number line, numbers get smaller as you go left. Taking away makes a number smaller, so you move left.

faq.q: How can I check a take-away sum?
faq.a: Hop forward again. 9 plus 6 brings you back to 15, so 15 take away 6 must be 9.

facts: Subtraction can be shown as hops to the left on a number line.

quiz.say: Start at 12 and hop back 4. Where do you land?
quiz.show: Start at 12 and hop back 4. Where do you land?

wrong.1: 9 counts the starting 12 as a hop.
wrong.2: 16 hops forward, which adds instead of taking away.

quiz.say: Which is a good way to do 14 minus 5?
quiz.show: Which is a good way to do 14 − 5?
quiz.why: 14 back 4 is 10, and back 1 more is 9: that is 5 hops back in all.

wrong.2: Starting at 10 is the wrong start; that gives 5.
